title: Mini Project: Employee Role Hierarchy
summary: Build a production-grade enterprise Employee Role Hierarchy system in Java, combining single, multilevel, and hierarchical inheritance with strict encapsulation and constructor chaining.
learningObjectives: Design and implement a multi-tier enterprise role hierarchy: Employee -> Developer, Manager, Executive
Apply constructor chaining with super() ensuring all parent invariants and IDs are strictly established
Enforce proper member access using private, protected, and public scopes across the hierarchy
Implement specialized role capabilities: code review metrics, team budget allocation, and executive stock grants
expectedOutcomes: A portfolio-ready, multi-class object-oriented inheritance engine in Java
Complete mastery over constructor propagation, state accumulation, and role specialization

activities.title: The Global Tech Corporation Organizational Architecture
activities.content:
In a global technology enterprise, every person on payroll has universal core attributes: a Corporate Badge ID, a Legal Name, a Department, and a Base Annual Salary.

However, their actual responsibilities and compensation structures diverge sharply based on their role in the company:
- **Software Engineers**: have programming languages, code review quotas, and engineering bonus pools.
- **Engineering Managers**: have direct reports, quarterly team budget authority, and hiring targets.
- **Senior Executives (VPs/Directors)**: have company-wide profit-sharing, equity stock options, and board reporting.

Notice the architecture: An Executive IS-A Manager, a Manager IS-A Employee. Software Engineers and Managers are sibling specializations of the base Employee. Building this in Java requires blending **single**, **multilevel**, and **hierarchical** inheritance into one cohesive corporate engine.

activities.title: System Architecture & 10-Point Production Blueprint
activities.content:
This mini-project combines all principles of Module 5 into an authentic enterprise compensation and role dispatch system.

### 1. Class Hierarchy Blueprint:
```
                    +-------------------+
                    |     Employee      | (Base Class)
                    |-------------------|
                    | - id: String      |
                    | - name: String    |
                    | - salary: double  |
                    +-------------------+
                              ^
                              |
               +--------------+--------------+
               |                             |
     +-------------------+         +-------------------+
     |     Developer     |         |      Manager      | (Siblings)
     |-------------------|         |-------------------|
     | - lang: String    |         | - teamSize: int   |
     | - bugFixes: int   |         | - budget: double  |
     +-------------------+         +-------------------+
                                             ^
                                             |
                                   +-------------------+
                                   |     Director      | (Multilevel Child)
                                   |-------------------|
                                   | - stockUnits: int |
                                   +-------------------+
```

### 2. The 10 Architectural Requirements:
1. **Base Employee**: Encapsulates `empId`, `name`, `baseSalary` with validation (salary must be positive).
2. **Super Constructor Chaining**: Every subclass constructor forwards parameters to `super()` on line 1.
3. **Field Protection**: Shared fields use `protected` or provide public getters to enforce encapsulation.
4. **Developer Role**: Adds `primaryLanguage` and `bugsResolved`, with a `resolveBug()` operation.
5. **Manager Role**: Adds `teamSize` and `annualTeamBudget`, with `allocateBudget()` checks.
6. **Director Role**: Extends `Manager` (multilevel), adding `stockUnits` and executive compensation bonuses.
7. **Annual Package Computation**: Each role computes total compensation combining base salary, team allowances, and equity grants.
8. **Clean Sibling Separation**: Developer and Manager remain strictly isolated with independent APIs.
9. **Execution Tracing**: Audited constructor execution logs verify top-down initialization.
10. **Zero Diamond Collision**: Single inheritance guarantees unambiguous method and variable lookup.

activities.title: The Complete Employee Role Hierarchy Engine
activities.description: Trace the full runnable multi-tier corporate role engine in Java.

steps.description: Employee provides baseline state (empId, name, baseSalary) with salary validation.
Developer extends Employee as a sibling, adding language and performance bonus calculations.
Manager extends Employee, introducing team size and budget oversight.
Director extends Manager (multilevel), accumulating Employee state, Manager state, and executive equity units.
Constructor chaining reliably establishes invariants through super() up to Employee.

activities.title: Mastery Verification: Employee Role Hierarchy Project (10 Questions)

questions.question: What type of inheritance relationship exists between Developer and Employee?
options: Single inheritance (and part of a hierarchical tree with Manager)
questions.explanation: Developer directly extends Employee as a single inheritance, forming a hierarchical tree alongside sibling Manager.

questions.question: What type of inheritance relationship exists between Director and Employee?
questions.explanation: Director extends Manager, which extends Employee, forming a 3-level multilevel inheritance chain.

questions.question: Where must the call to super(id, name, salary) be placed in the Developer constructor?
options: As the very first statement on line 1
questions.explanation: Java mandates that super() constructor calls must be the very first statement.

questions.question: Can a Developer instance access the teamBudget field of a Manager instance?
options: No, sibling classes have strict isolation and cannot access each other's specialized members
questions.explanation: Sibling isolation guarantees that Developer and Manager have zero access to each other's specialized fields.

questions.question: Can Director access the teamBudget field of Manager?
options: No, only Employee fields are accessible
Yes, because Director is a child of Manager and teamBudget is protected
questions.explanation: Director is a subclass of Manager, so it directly inherits all protected and public members of Manager.

questions.question: If Developer declares 'double baseSalary = 0;', what happens to Employee's baseSalary?
options: It is shadowed in Developer; both fields exist in the heap object
questions.explanation: Declaring a field with the same name in a subclass shadows the parent field. Both exist in memory.

questions.question: How can Director invoke Manager's calculateTotalCompensation() method?
questions.explanation: 'super.calculateTotalCompensation()' calls the immediate parent's implementation directly.

questions.question: When 'new Director(...)' is called, which constructor body finishes executing first?
questions.explanation: Constructor bodies execute from the top of the inheritance tree downward: Object finishes first, followed by Employee, Manager, and finally Director.

questions.question: Why should baseSalary in Employee be private or protected instead of public?
options: To prevent outside classes from corrupting salary values and bypassing validation rules
Because Java prohibits public variables in classes
To make the code run twice as fast
questions.explanation: Encapsulation prevents unauthorized mutation and ensures salary validation invariants are preserved.

questions.question: What is the primary architectural takeaway from this project?
options: Inheritance should be nested at least 10 levels deep
Combining single, multilevel, and hierarchical inheritance creates clean, maintainable real-world models without code duplication
Always use public fields in inheritance
Never use constructors in child classes
questions.explanation: Clean object-oriented inheritance models complex corporate domain relationships with zero code duplication and high reliability.

activities.title: Interview Essentials: Employee Role Hierarchy Project

interviewQA.question: How does this Employee Role Hierarchy demonstrate the combination of hierarchical and multilevel inheritance?
interviewQA.answer: Hierarchical inheritance is demonstrated where Employee is the single superclass branching into sibling subclasses Developer and Manager. Multilevel inheritance is demonstrated where Director extends Manager, which extends Employee. The system blends both patterns to model organizational depth and specialization cleanly.

interviewQA.question: Walk through the constructor chaining sequence when an instance of Director is created.
interviewQA.answer: When 'new Director()' is called: 1. Director constructor calls 'super()' on line 1. 2. Manager constructor calls 'super()' on line 1. 3. Employee constructor calls implicit 'super()' to java.lang.Object. 4. Object constructor executes. 5. Employee constructor initializes empId, name, salary. 6. Manager constructor initializes teamSize, budget. 7. Director constructor initializes stockUnits. The execution order is strictly top-down.

interviewQA.question: How is sibling isolation maintained between Developer and Manager?
interviewQA.answer: Developer and Manager are separate classes in the type system with no inheritance relationship between them. Developer has no access to teamSize or teamBudget, and Manager has no access to primaryLanguage or bugsResolved. A Developer reference cannot be assigned to a Manager variable.

interviewQA.question: Why is 'super.calculateTotalCompensation()' used in Director rather than recalculating from scratch?
interviewQA.answer: Calling 'super.calculateTotalCompensation()' adheres to the DRY principle. Manager already contains verified logic for calculating base salary plus team management bonus. Director reuses that existing calculation and simply augments it with executive equity compensation.

interviewQA.question: What happens if Employee has only a 3-argument constructor, and a developer forgets super(...) in Developer?
interviewQA.answer: The code will not compile. Without an explicit 'super(...)', the Java compiler attempts to insert an implicit zero-argument 'super();'. Because Employee has a custom constructor, no default constructor exists, causing a 'constructor Employee() is undefined' compile-time error.

interviewQA.question: How would you extend this architecture to support Contract Workers who are not salaried?
interviewQA.answer: You could extract an interface 'Payable' or create an abstract base class 'Worker' with common identity (id, name), from which 'SalariedEmployee' and 'ContractWorker' branch hierarchically. ContractWorker would define hourlyRate and hoursLogged rather than an annual base salary.

activities.title: Module 5 Capstone Self-Evaluation Checklist
checklist: Base Employee class properly encapsulates id, name, and baseSalary with validation
Developer and Manager extend Employee as sibling subclasses with isolated state
Director extends Manager as a multilevel subclass accumulating all ancestor state
All subclass constructors invoke super(...) as the very first statement on line 1
calculateTotalCompensation correctly computes role-specific bonuses across all tiers
No compilation errors caused by missing parent zero-argument constructors
Sibling isolation is preserved (Developer cannot access Manager members)
Shadowed fields and methods are safely resolved using super where appropriate
Inheritance hierarchy remains shallow (3 levels max) to avoid fragile base class issues
The complete role hierarchy compiles and executes with 100% verified test cases

practiceProblems.description: Construct a 3-tier hierarchy: Employee -> Manager -> Director with executive equity compensation.
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Build Employee -> Manager -> Director. Director extends Manager, adding restrictedStockUnits (int) and sharePriceUsd (double). Implement computeExecutiveWealth() returning computeAnnualCompensation() + (restrictedStockUnits * sharePriceUsd). From scratch.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput: Executive Director DIR-01 (Marcus Brody) Total Wealth: $325000.0 (Equity Value: $150000.0)

Call super(id, name, salary, dept, reports) on line 1.

practiceProblems.title: Fix Broken Code: Constructor Chaining Crash in Role Hierarchy
practiceProblems.description: Fix a compilation failure caused by child constructor missing parent arguments.
practiceProblems.problemStatement: The code fails to compile because Employee has no zero-arg constructor, and LeadDeveloper did not pass name or salary to super(). Fix the constructor chaining.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput: Lead Developer Ada Lovelace leading Backend (Salary: $125000.0)
hints: Add super(name, salary); as the very first line of LeadDeveloper constructor.

Total Enterprise Payroll: $415000.0

Iterate and sum calculateTotalCompensation() across all employees.
